The write-up's Sources line lists exactly these four works: Raman, Wierzbicki & Fournier (2026); Panickssery et al. (2024); Turner et al. (2023); Okafor, Tanaka & Aaltonen (2026).

message_source_quote: The reading list's Raman et al. 2026 (white-bear steering) is the direct prior: a two-sided think-vs-don't-think stance contrast (concept present in both arms) at L20–24 makes implied concepts J-lens-readable.
writeup_source_quote: This differs from white-bear steering (Raman et al. 2026), which contrasts *think about X* with *don't think about X*: there the concept is present in both arms, so its direction is a *stance* direction, and the don't-think arm still activates the concept (the white-bear effect).

differences.what: The message discloses a decomposition analysis showing that the WBS-collinear component of the one-sided direction carries the empirical gain, which bears on how novel/independent the one-sided method's improvement actually is relative to white-bear steering; the write-up contains no such analysis or caveat.
differences.message_quote: A decomposition (direction minus its WBS projection) showed the WBS-collinear component carries the gain, which I did not overclaim in the write-up

differences.what: The message states that reproducing the white-bear steering method was explicitly out of scope and that a WBS-equivalent control was built only to validate mechanism/calibrate dose, framing the relationship to the source as a deliberately bounded comparison; the write-up presents the two-sided comparison simply as a performance contrast (0.7843 vs 0.5882) without this scoping context.
differences.message_quote: Reproducing it is explicitly out of scope, so I used a WBS-equivalent control (rebuilt from the DM dev items) only to validate the mechanism and calibrate dose/position.
differences.writeup_quote: At the same per-layer dose the one-sided direction outperforms the two-sided white-bear direction (0.7843 vs 0.5882).

rationale: Both documents treat Raman et al. 2026 (white-bear steering) as the explicit, named prior that the submitted one-sided method differs from along the same stance-vs-activation axis, and both report the identical headline comparison (0.7843 one-sided vs 0.5882 two-sided WBS) as the novelty evidence, so their core source/novelty framing is equal. The message adds two things absent from the write-up: an explicit 'out of scope to reproduce' framing of the source relationship, and a decomposition finding suggesting the gain is partly WBS-collinear, which slightly complicates the novelty story the write-up tells cleanly.
